facts.raw_span: A 56-year-old man presented with a 2-month history of bitemporal hemianopia and left labial numbness
visual impairment, bitemporal hemianopia, and right abducens nerve palsy

Pituitary MRI demonstrated diffuse swelling of the pituitary body and stalk, a 7-mm poorly enhancing mass in the right anterior lobe, loss of the posterior pituitary bright spot on T1-weighted images, and thickening of the sphenoid sinus mucosa
Serum IgG4 was elevated at 319 mg/dL
A 56-year-old man presented with a 2-month history of bitemporal hemianopia and left labial numbness
visual impairment, bitemporal hemianopia, and right abducens nerve palsy

Pituitary MRI demonstrated diffuse swelling of the pituitary body and stalk, a 7-mm poorly enhancing mass in the right anterior lobe, loss of the posterior pituitary bright spot on T1-weighted images, and thickening of the sphenoid sinus mucosa
Serum IgG4 was elevated at 319 mg/dL

concepts.why: The patient's presentation with bitemporal hemianopia, hypopituitarism, and elevated IgG4 levels, along with pituitary MRI findings, supports this diagnosis.
The presence of a 7-mm poorly enhancing mass in the right anterior lobe on pituitary MRI suggests a pituitary adenoma.
The patient's elevated IgG4 levels and presence of a lung nodular lesion on chest CT support this diagnosis.
The patient's laboratory results show multiple hormonal deficiencies, consistent with hypopituitarism.
The patient's presentation with right abducens nerve palsy supports this diagnosis.
The patient's pituitary MRI shows thickening of the sphenoid sinus mucosa, suggesting sphenoid sinusitis.
The patient's chest CT shows a nodular lesion in the left lung field, consistent with a lung nodule.
The patient's laboratory results show cortisol and ACTH levels consistent with adrenal insufficiency.

rationales.F01: Initial presentation of bitemporal hemianopia and left labial numbness suggests a pituitary issue, but is not specific enough to rule in or out any particular diagnosis.
rationales.F02: Visual impairment, bitemporal hemianopia, and right abducens nerve palsy are consistent with a pituitary lesion, and the abducens nerve palsy is a strong indicator of this.
rationales.F09: Low cortisol level is a strong indicator of adrenal insufficiency.
rationales.F11: Pituitary MRI findings are highly suggestive of IgG4-related hypophysitis, and also support the diagnosis of hypopituitarism and a possible pituitary adenoma.
rationales.F12: Elevated IgG4 level is a strong indicator of IgG4-related disease, including IgG4-related hypophysitis and systemic IgG4-related disease.
